title: Product of Array Except Self
description: Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `output` where `output[i]` equals the product of all elements of `nums` except `nums[i]`. It must run in O(n) time and **must not use division**. Every prefix and suffix product fits in a 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: Any position other than the zero includes the zero in its product.

constraints: Prefix and suffix products fit in a 32-bit integer
hints: Without division and with zeros possible, you can't just divide the total by nums[i]. Split the product around index i instead.
output[i] = (product of everything to the left of i) * (product of everything to the right of i).
Fill the output with running left products in one pass, then sweep right-to-left multiplying in a running right product.
starterCode:

solution.explanation: The product excluding index i is the product of everything left of i times everything right of i. A first pass stores in `res[i]` the product of all earlier elements. A second pass from the right keeps a running product of later elements and multiplies it into `res[i]`. Two linear passes give O(n) time, and apart from the output array we use only a couple of variables, so extra space is O(1).
